base_instance_name.description: The base instance name to use for instances in this group. The value must be a valid RFC1035 name. Supported characters are lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens (-). Instances are named by appending a hyphen and a random four-character string to the base instance name.
base_instance_name.rationale: Just a naming prefix for instances. No security impact.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Only controls whether Terraform's own destroy/apply workflow is allowed to remove the resource - it has no effect on the deployed GCE resource's actual security posture, and it can still be deleted via gcloud/console/another Terraform state regardless of this setting. Forcing 'PREVENT' platform-wide would also block legitimate CI/CD pipelines that need automated teardown of ephemeral environments. IaC-workflow safety guard, not a security control.

description.description: An optional textual description of the instance group manager.
description.rationale: Just a free-text note for humans. Doesn't affect security.

list_managed_instances_results.description: Pagination behavior of the listManagedInstances API method for this managed instance group. Valid values are: "PAGELESS", "PAGINATED". If PAGELESS (default), Pagination is disabled for the group's listManagedInstances API method. maxResults and pageToken query parameters are ignored and all instances are returned in a single response. If PAGINATED, pagination is enabled, maxResults and pageToken query parameters are respected.
list_managed_instances_results.rationale: Just controls how API results are paginated. Not a security setting.

name.description: The name of the instance group manager. Must be 1-63 characters long and comply with RFC1035. Supported characters include lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens.
name.rationale: Just the resource's name. No security impact.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Just says which project owns the resource. No security impact.

target_pools.description: The full URL of all target pools to which new instances in the group are added. Updating the target pools attribute does not affect existing instances.
target_pools.rationale: Just points to target pools. We'd secure those pools on their own, not which ones are linked here.

target_size.description: The target number of running instances for this managed instance group. This value should always be explicitly set unless this resource is attached to an autoscaler, in which case it should never be set. Defaults to 0.
target_size.rationale: Just how many instances to run. Not a security setting.

target_stopped_size.description: The target number of stopped instances for this managed instance group.
target_stopped_size.rationale: Just how many instances to keep stopped. Not a security setting.

target_suspended_size.description: The target number of suspended instances for this managed instance group.
target_suspended_size.rationale: Just how many instances to keep suspended. Not a security setting.

wait_for_instances.description: Whether to wait for all instances to be created/updated before returning. Note that if this is set to true and the operation does not succeed, Terraform will continue trying until it times out.
wait_for_instances.rationale: Just controls whether Terraform waits for instances to finish before returning. Doesn't affect the resource's security.

wait_for_instances_status.description: When used with wait_for_instances specifies the status to wait for. When STABLE is specified this resource will wait until the instances are stable before returning. When UPDATED is set, it will wait for the version target to be reached and any per instance configs to be effective and all instances configs to be effective as well as all instances to be stable before returning.
wait_for_instances_status.rationale: Just which status Terraform waits for. Doesn't affect the resource's security.

zone.description: The zone that instances in this group should be created in.
zone.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

all_instances_config.description: Specifies configuration that overrides the instance template configuration for the group.

all_instances_config.labels.description: The label key-value pairs that you want to patch onto the instance,
all_instances_config.labels.rationale: Just tags for organizing. No security impact.

all_instances_config.metadata.description: The metadata key-value pairs that you want to patch onto the instance. For more information, see Project and instance metadata,
all_instances_config.metadata.rationale: Sets metadata on the instances, which includes reserved GCE keys with real hardening semantics (enable-oslogin, block-project-ssh-keys, serial-port-enable). A policy should discourage turning those protections off.

auto_healing_policies.description: The autohealing policies for this managed instance group. You can specify only one value.

auto_healing_policies.health_check.description: The health check resource that signals autohealing.
auto_healing_policies.health_check.rationale: Just points to a health check. We'd secure that health check on its own, not which one is linked here.

auto_healing_policies.initial_delay_sec.description: The number of seconds that the managed instance group waits before it applies autohealing policies to new instances or recently recreated instances. Between 0 and 3600.
auto_healing_policies.initial_delay_sec.rationale: Sets the grace period before the group starts acting on an instance that's failing its health check. It's an availability tuning knob (how quickly to react to a bad instance), not a security control.

instance_lifecycle_policy.description: The instance lifecycle policy for this managed instance group.

instance_lifecycle_policy.default_action.description: Default behavior for all instance or health check failures.
instance_lifecycle_policy.default_action.rationale: Decides how the group recovers an instance after it or its health check fails. This is about keeping the app running (availability), not about securing it.

instance_lifecycle_policy.force_update_o.description: Specifies whether to apply the group's latest configuration when repairing a VM. Valid options are: YES, NO. If YES and you updated the group's instance template or per-instance configurations after the VM was created, then these changes are applied when VM is repaired. If NO (default), then updates are applied in accordance with the group's update policy type.
instance_lifecycle_policy.force_update_o.rationale: Decides whether a VM repair rebuilds the instance from the group's latest template/config, or keeps whatever it already had. It's an operational lifecycle choice about staying up to date, not a security control.

named_port.name.rationale: Just a label naming a port mapping for the load balancer. It's descriptive only and doesn't enforce anything, so no security impact.

named_port.port.rationale: Sets the port number the load balancer routes traffic to on each instance. Which ports can actually be reached from outside is governed by firewall rules, not this mapping.

resource_policies.description: Resource policies for this managed instance group.

resource_policies.workload_policy.description: The URL of the workload policy that is specified for this managed instance group. It can be a full or partial URL.
resource_policies.workload_policy.rationale: Points to a workload policy resource. We'd secure that referenced policy's own settings directly, not police which policy this group happens to point at.

standby_policy.description: Standby policy for stopped and suspended instances.

standby_policy.initial_delay_sec.description: Specifies the number of seconds that the MIG should wait to suspend or stop a VM after that VM was created. The initial delay gives the initialization script the time to prepare your VM for a quick scale out. The value of initial delay must be between 0 and 3600 seconds. The default value is 0.
standby_policy.initial_delay_sec.rationale: A timeout delay before a standby VM is suspended or stopped, giving its startup script time to finish. It's purely about scale-out timing, not security.

standby_policy.mode.description: Defines how a MIG resumes or starts VMs from a standby pool when the group scales out. The default mode is "MANUAL".
standby_policy.mode.rationale: Chooses how standby instances resume during scale-out (manual vs automatic). Every option, including the 'MANUAL' default, is equally safe - it only affects scale-out behavior, not the resource's security.

stateful_disk.description: Disks created on the instances that will be preserved on instance delete, update, etc.

stateful_disk.delete_rule.description: A value that prescribes what should happen to the stateful disk when the VM instance is deleted. The available options are NEVER and ON_PERMANENT_INSTANCE_DELETION. NEVER - detach the disk when the VM is deleted, but do not delete the disk. ON_PERMANENT_INSTANCE_DELETION will delete the stateful disk when the VM is permanently deleted from the instance group. The default is NEVER.
stateful_disk.delete_rule.rationale: Just decides whether a disk is kept or deleted when an instance goes away. A data-management choice, not a security setting.

stateful_disk.device_name.description: The device name of the disk to be attached.
stateful_disk.device_name.rationale: Just the disk's device name. No security impact.

stateful_external_ip.description: External IPs considered stateful by the instance group.

stateful_external_ip.delete_rule.description: A value that prescribes what should happen to an associated static Address resource when a VM instance is permanently deleted. The available options are NEVER and ON_PERMANENT_INSTANCE_DELETION. NEVER - detach the IP when the VM is deleted, but do not delete the address resource. ON_PERMANENT_INSTANCE_DELETION will delete the stateful address when the VM is permanently deleted from the instance group. The default is NEVER.
stateful_external_ip.delete_rule.rationale: Just decides whether an external IP is kept or deleted when an instance goes away. A data-management choice, not a security setting.

stateful_external_ip.interface_name.rationale: Just the network interface's name. No security impact.

stateful_internal_ip.description: External IPs considered stateful by the instance group.

stateful_internal_ip.delete_rule.description: A value that prescribes what should happen to an associated static Address resource when a VM instance is permanently deleted. The available options are NEVER and ON_PERMANENT_INSTANCE_DELETION. NEVER - detach the IP when the VM is deleted, but do not delete the address resource. ON_PERMANENT_INSTANCE_DELETION will delete the stateful address when the VM is permanently deleted from the instance group. The default is NEVER.
stateful_internal_ip.delete_rule.rationale: Just decides whether an internal IP is kept or deleted when an instance goes away. A data-management choice, not a security setting.

stateful_internal_ip.interface_name.rationale: Just the network interface's name. No security impact.

target_size_policy.description: The policy that specifies how the MIG creates its VMs to achieve the target size.

target_size_policy.mode.description: The mode of target size policy based on which the MIG creates its VMs individually or all at once.
target_size_policy.mode.rationale: Just decides how VMs are created (one at a time or all at once). Not a security setting.

update_policy.description: The update policy for this managed instance group.

update_policy.max_surge_fixed.description: Specifies a fixed number of VM instances. This must be a positive integer. Conflicts with max_surge_percent. Both cannot be 0
update_policy.max_surge_fixed.rationale: Just how many extra instances to create during a rollout. Not a security setting.

update_policy.max_surge_percent.description: Specifies a percentage of instances between 0 to 100%, inclusive. For example, specify 80 for 80%. Conflicts with max_surge_fixed.
update_policy.max_surge_percent.rationale: Sets how many extra instances (as a %) can be created during a rollout. Every value here, including leaving it unset, only trades off rollout speed for capacity - it doesn't weaken the resource's security.

update_policy.max_unavailable_fixed.description: Specifies a fixed number of VM instances. This must be a positive integer.
update_policy.max_unavailable_fixed.rationale: Sets how many instances (as a fixed count) can be offline at once during a rollout. Every value here, including leaving it unset, only trades off rollout speed for availability - it doesn't weaken the resource's security.

update_policy.max_unavailable_percent.description: Specifies a percentage of instances between 0 to 100%, inclusive. For example, specify 80 for 80%.
update_policy.max_unavailable_percent.rationale: Sets how many instances (as a %) can be offline at once during a rollout. Every value here, including leaving it unset, only trades off rollout speed for availability - it doesn't weaken the resource's security.

update_policy.minimal_action.description: Minimal action to be taken on an instance. You can specify either NONE to forbid any actions, REFRESH to update without stopping instances, RESTART to restart existing instances or REPLACE to delete and create new instances from the target template. If you specify a REFRESH, the Updater will attempt to perform that action only. However, if the Updater determines that the minimal action you specify is not enough to perform the update, it might perform a more disruptive action.
update_policy.minimal_action.rationale: Sets the smallest action Terraform tries first during an update (e.g. refresh vs restart vs replace). Every option, including the default, is equally safe - it only affects how disruptive an update is, not the resource's security.

update_policy.most_disruptive_allowed_ac.description: Most disruptive action that is allowed to be taken on an instance. You can specify either NONE to forbid any actions, REFRESH to allow actions that do not need instance restart, RESTART to allow actions that can be applied without instance replacing or REPLACE to allow all possible actions. If the Updater determines that the minimal update action needed is more disruptive than most disruptive allowed action you specify it will not perform the update at all.
update_policy.most_disruptive_allowed_ac.rationale: Caps how disruptive an update is allowed to get (e.g. never fully replace an instance). Every option, including the default, is equally safe - it only limits rollout disruption, not the resource's security.

update_policy.replacement_method.description: The instance replacement method for managed instance groups. Valid values are: "RECREATE", "SUBSTITUTE". If SUBSTITUTE (default), the group replaces VM instances with new instances that have randomly generated names. If RECREATE, instance names are preserved.  You must also set max_unavailable_fixed or max_unavailable_percent to be greater than 0.
update_policy.replacement_method.rationale: Chooses whether replaced instances keep their original name or get a new randomly-generated one. Every option, including the 'SUBSTITUTE' default, is equally safe - it's a naming/rollout detail, not a security control.

update_policy.type.description: The type of update process. You can specify either PROACTIVE so that the instance group manager proactively executes actions in order to bring instances to their target versions or OPPORTUNISTIC so that no action is proactively executed but the update will be performed as part of other actions (for example, resizes or recreateInstances calls).
update_policy.type.rationale: Controls when instance updates actually get applied. 'PROACTIVE' has the group push out template/config changes to instances on its own; 'OPPORTUNISTIC' waits and only applies them as a side effect of some other action (like a resize). Neither option changes what gets deployed or how the instance is secured - it only changes the timing/scheduling of the rollout, which is a deployment-pacing choice, not a security control.

version.description: Application versions managed by this instance group. Each version deals with a specific instance template, allowing canary release scenarios.

version.instance_template.description: The full URL to an instance template from which all new instances of this version will be created.
version.instance_template.rationale: Just points to an instance template. We'd secure that template on its own, not which one is linked here.

version.name.rationale: Just a label for the version. No security impact.

version.target_size.description: The number of instances calculated as a fixed number or a percentage depending on the settings.

version.target_size.fixed.description: The number of instances which are managed for this version. Conflicts with percent.
version.target_size.fixed.rationale: Just how many instances to run for this version. Not a security setting.

version.target_size.percent.description: The number of instances (calculated as percentage) which are managed for this version. Conflicts with fixed. Note that when using percent, rounding will be in favor of explicitly set target_size values; a managed instance group with 2 instances and 2 versions, one of which has a target_size.percent of 60 will create 2 instances of that version.
version.target_size.percent.rationale: Just what percentage of instances to run for this version. Not a security setting.
